summary: A ticketed ($29-$34) workshop and cacao ceremony hosted by a single named practitioner, Priscilla Jordan, at Asia House Asheville. Only two sessions were listed 3 months apart, with 'Red Tent' and 'sacred circle' used as marketing language rather than as the name of an established, independently branded community. No membership language, group name, or dedicated web/social presence for the group was found.

evidence.note: Ticketed Eventbrite listing ($29-$34) by organizer Priscilla Jordan; description markets the session's content (cacao, yoga, dance, 'sacred song circle') rather than describing a returning membership or naming the group itself.

Second listing 3 months earlier, same organizer, same generic 'RED TENT WORKSHOP & CACAO CEREMONY' title reused rather than a distinct standing group name; page footer says 'STAY TUNED FOR OUR SPRING WORKSHOPS!' implying an occasional workshop series, not a chartered ongoing circle.
No 'members', 'our group', dues, sign-up form, Facebook group, Meetup, or Discord link appears in either listing; only the host's Eventbrite 'more events' link is referenced.

WebSearch was unavailable (session search budget exhausted) and WebFetch against Google/DuckDuckGo search result pages returned only CAPTCHA/error pages, so no independent website, Facebook page, or news coverage for Priscilla Jordan or a 'Red Tent Asheville' group could be located.

Sparse cadence (2 events, ~91 day median gap) and per-session ticket pricing pattern-match a practitioner-run paid workshop rather than a self-sustaining circle with a fixed, recognizable core of returning attendees.
